newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes thin but refiners relaxed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes thin but refiners relaxed.

text.p: U.S. foreign crudes stayed thin in slow Tuesday trade, with refiners relaxed about a drop in trans-Atlantic imports due to ample domestic supplies.
A narrow arbitrage virtually choked off supplies from the North Sea, evidenced by crude imports falling to 6.5 million barrels per day in the American Petroleum Institute report.
Imports fell 760,000 barrels per day from the previous week and were only recently above 8.0 million bpd.
But refiners said domestic crudes were ample and extra barrels from Latin America were being offered, amid also more sour crude sales from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR).
A U.S. refiner offered Oriente loading end October, but asked on an fob basis, formula related.
Traders said the value of Oriente cif was around WTI minus $2.00-2.05, weaker than last month's minus $1.80 level.
But lighter grades were faring better with Cusiana asked around Nov WTI parity for a mid October loader, while Vasconia was asked at WTI minus $1.85/1.90 fob, loading later Oct.
Meanwhile, a trader bringing Brent to the Gulf Coast for early Oct was believed to have sold out, with last barrels going for Nov WTI plus five to 10 cents cif.
Further, a U.S. refiner bought an 80,000 tonne cargo of Alba crude for early November arrival, but price was not immediately available.
Traders expect distillate-rich grades to remain supported against diminished values for heavier crudes.
In the U.S. after market, Nov Brent traded at $23.18 and $23.23 a barrel, up from the IPE settlement of $23.07.
Intermonth Nov/Dec Brent traded twice at 44 and 46 cents, fluctuating within London's earlier trading range.
